title: Bare-Metal Provisioning in Plain English
summary: Understand how VMM can turn an approved physical server into a managed Hyper-V host without confusing discovery, imaging and production acceptance.
plain_language_explanation: VMM bare-metal deployment is a controlled build pipeline. The server is discovered through its hardware-management interface, started through PXE, configured from a physical computer profile, installed with Windows Server and Hyper-V, and finally added to the VMM fabric. A completed deployment job does not by itself prove firmware, network, storage, clustering or workload readiness.
quick_check: Why should a successfully imaged host still pass independent production acceptance checks before workloads are placed on it?

title: PXE, BMC Discovery and Physical Computer Profiles
summary: Design the prerequisites that let VMM discover, boot and consistently provision physical Hyper-V hosts.
objective: Explain how PXE, out-of-band management and physical computer profiles combine into a repeatable host-build workflow.
body_outline: Bare-metal provisioning depends on supported BMC/out-of-band management, a reachable PXE service and hardware configured to boot from the network in the approved sequence.
Adding a PXE server to VMM installs the VMM agent on that Windows Deployment Services server and makes PXE a managed fabric resource.

A physical computer profile defines host-build settings such as operating-system image, product and identity settings, disk layout, drivers, network configuration, host group and post-deployment behavior.
BMC credentials and PXE reachability are privileged infrastructure dependencies and should be separated from normal operator credentials.
DNS, DHCP/PXE boundaries, VLANs, driver currency and firmware state must be reconciled with the physical design before deployment begins.
Discovery success is not production acceptance; firmware, storage paths, networking, cluster validation and security baselines remain separate gates.

title: SCVMM Host Compliance, Maintenance Mode and Cluster Servicing
summary: Operate managed Hyper-V hosts through compliance baselines, maintenance windows and cluster-aware servicing without confusing VMM orchestration with host health.
objective: Build a production-safe operating model for VMM-managed host patching and maintenance.
body_outline: VMM can integrate a WSUS server, assign update baselines and report compliance for managed hosts and clusters.
Maintenance mode is an operational state for planned host work; it does not replace workload evacuation, cluster-health checks or change control.
For clustered Hyper-V hosts, servicing must preserve quorum, capacity reserve, CSV/storage access and network availability while nodes are maintained.
VMM servicing windows are scheduling metadata; they do not themselves execute maintenance or prevent unsafe external changes.
A host returning to OK in VMM should still be checked for cluster membership, live-migration capability, storage/network paths and expected workload placement.
Remediation is a change action. Discovery and audit labs should remain read-only and escalate noncompliance rather than silently patching production hosts.

title: SCVMM Host Lifecycle Control Plane: Build, Admit, Service and Reconcile
summary: Connect bare-metal provisioning, host admission, cluster operations and servicing into one evidence-driven lifecycle.
architecture_notes: A production host passes through several different control planes: hardware/BMC, PXE and imaging, Windows/Hyper-V, VMM fabric, failover clustering, storage/network fabrics and finally workload placement. Treating these as one green-or-red status hides failure domains. The operating model should preserve evidence at each boundary and require explicit admission criteria before automation is allowed to place workloads.
failure_modes: PXE responds but the wrong image/profile is selected
BMC discovery succeeds while firmware or BIOS policy is noncompliant
host joins VMM but logical-network mappings do not match physical VLANs
host is patched but cluster capacity or CSV state is unsafe
maintenance mode is cleared before storage/network paths recover
VMM compliance is green while an external patching system changed unsupported components
a rebuilt host is treated as identical without reconciling identity, certificates and security state
enterprise_design_notes: Use lifecycle gates: hardware readiness, deployment readiness, fabric admission, cluster admission, workload admission, maintenance entry, maintenance exit and post-change reconciliation. Each gate should have evidence, owner and rollback boundary.

title: Read-Only SCVMM Host Lifecycle Discovery Pack
summary: Inventory PXE, host, cluster and compliance state without deploying a host, changing BMC/PXE configuration or remediating updates.
objective: Produce a timestamped lifecycle evidence pack before any host deployment, patch remediation or maintenance-mode change is approved.
steps: Record VMM server identity and current fabric status.
Inventory registered PXE servers and record their reported state without adding or repairing them.
Inventory managed Hyper-V hosts and clusters, including operating-system and agent metadata.
Record current host status, cluster membership and available maintenance/compliance metadata without invoking refresh, repair or remediation.
Compare representative hosts with approved build, network, storage and cluster-design records.
Document mismatches, stale state and missing evidence as findings rather than correcting them during discovery.
expected_result: A read-only lifecycle inventory and mismatch register with no bare-metal deployment, BMC/PXE mutation, patch remediation, maintenance-mode change or workload movement.

title: SCVMM Bare-Metal or Host-Servicing Incident Decision Tree
summary: Separate hardware, PXE, image/profile, VMM-agent, cluster and compliance failures before attempting destructive recovery steps.
diagnostic_order: Classify the failure as BMC/out-of-band discovery, PXE/WDS, image/profile, driver/network, VMM-agent, host admission, cluster admission or compliance/servicing issue.
Preserve VMM job IDs, hardware identity and deployment logs before retrying a failed bare-metal workflow.
Confirm DHCP/PXE and BMC reachability from the approved management boundaries without changing boot order, firmware or credentials.
For an already managed host, prove Hyper-V and failover-cluster health independently of VMM before treating the issue as a VMM defect.
If maintenance or remediation failed, verify workload evacuation, node state, CSV/storage, network paths and cluster capacity before returning the node to service.
Escalate when resolution requires reimaging, BMC reset, PXE modification, agent repair, cluster membership changes or patch remediation.
escalation_boundary: Do not initiate bare-metal deployment, alter BMC credentials or firmware, add/remove PXE servers, reimage hosts, repair VMM agents, remediate update baselines, change maintenance mode, move workloads or modify cluster membership without approved change authority and rollback evidence.

title: SCVMM Bare-Metal Provisioning and Host Lifecycle Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering PXE/BMC prerequisites, physical computer profiles, host admission, compliance and safe servicing.

assessment_items.question: What three infrastructure elements are central to a VMM bare-metal host build?
assessment_items.answer: Out-of-band/BMC discovery, PXE/Windows PE boot and a physical computer profile that defines the approved host-build configuration.

assessment_items.question: Does a completed bare-metal deployment job prove the host is production ready?
assessment_items.answer: No. Host, cluster, storage, network, security and workload-admission checks are separate gates.

assessment_items.question: What does a VMM servicing window do?
assessment_items.answer: It provides scheduling metadata for maintenance; it does not itself execute maintenance or guarantee that a change is safe.

assessment_items.question: Why should update-baseline remediation be excluded from a read-only training lab?
assessment_items.answer: Remediation changes production hosts and can trigger maintenance and workload-availability consequences, so it requires explicit change authority and rollback planning.

title: Senior SCVMM Interview: Bare-Metal Provisioning and Host Lifecycle
summary: Senior production scenarios testing PXE/BMC design, physical profiles, host admission, cluster servicing and troubleshooting boundaries.

questions.question: A new server is visible through BMC but never reaches Windows PE. How do you structure the investigation?
answer_points: verify supported BMC protocol and credentials
confirm server identity and profile assignment
avoid repeated reimage attempts until the failing layer is known

questions.question: VMM reports a newly built host as OK. What evidence do you require before workload placement?
answer_points: cluster validation and membership if clustered

questions.question: A cluster node is noncompliant with updates. What should happen before remediation?
Why is a physical computer profile a governance artifact rather than just an imaging convenience?
answer_points: it standardizes OS and host build choices
profile changes affect future host builds
it should be versioned, reviewed and reconciled with hardware/security standards
